channel.title: Azure Functions on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in Azure Functions on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for Azure Functions OpenAI Extension ends on April 20, 2027
item.description:
Support for the Azure Functions OpenAI extension ends on April 20, 2027. Users should migrate to the appropriate direct SDKs before that date, including OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry, or Azure AI Search SDKs depending on the scenario.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Functions Network Troubleshooter v2
item.description:
Azure Functions Network Troubleshooter v2 is now in public preview. It provides a top-down view of Function App dependencies across Storage, Service Bus, and Azure Files, with inspection details for supported dependencies.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Functions support for Node.js 26
item.description:
Azure Functions now supports Node.js 26 in public preview. Developers can test JavaScript and TypeScript function apps on the new runtime while continuing to use the Azure Functions programming model on Linux in Flex Consumption and Elastic Premium plans.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Functions support for Python 3.15
item.description:
Azure Functions now has public preview support for Python 3.15. Developers can test Python apps, dependencies, native extensions, and deployment workflows with the existing v1 and v2 programming models.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Hosted Skill and Agent Bindings for Azure Functions
item.description:
Hosted Skill and Agent bindings for Azure Functions are in public preview. The bindings aim to reduce application plumbing and lifecycle code needed when adding agents, so developers can focus on business logic.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Native disaster recovery for Azure Functions durable task scheduler
item.description:
Azure Functions durable task scheduler now has public preview disaster recovery for the Dedicated SKU in supported Azure regions. It lets you recover workflow orchestration state after a regional outage without rebuilding it.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: OS-level dependency support via containers for Azure Functions Flex Consumption
item.description:
Azure Functions Flex Consumption now has preview support for OS-level dependencies via containers. This lets apps extend the Microsoft-managed worker environment with native executables and system libraries.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Task Queues for Azure Functions durable task scheduler
item.description:
Task Queues for Azure Functions durable task scheduler are in public preview. They let workloads sharing a task hub use named queues so you can separate throughput needs and downstream service limits.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Customer-managed keys for Azure Functions durable task scheduler
item.description:
Customer-managed keys for Azure Functions Durable Task Scheduler are now generally available for Dedicated SKU schedulers. This lets organizations use their own keys to encrypt workflow data.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Golang support on Azure Functions Flex Consumption
item.description:
Go support on Azure Functions Flex Consumption is now generally available. It provides a code-first model with typed Go handlers, standard Go modules, and integration with Azure Functions Core Tools and Azure CLI.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Managed Connectors in Azure Functions
item.description:
Managed connectors in Azure Functions are now generally available. They let developers build event-driven applications that respond to events and trigger actions across Microsoft 365, SaaS, and business systems using the Azure Functions programming model.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Private endpoints for Azure Functions durable task scheduler
item.description:
Private endpoints for Azure Functions durable task scheduler are now generally available. This supports both Dedicated and Consumption SKU schedulers, allowing Azure Functions and other durable task SDK workloads to connect to the scheduler over a private IP address.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Functions support for .NET 11
item.description:
Azure Functions support for .NET 11 is now generally available. You can build Functions apps targeting .NET 11 with the isolated worker model while continuing to use the Azure Functions programming model and host integration.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure Functions v1 hosting model on Azure Container Apps
item.description:
Azure Functions v1 hosting model on Azure Container Apps will be retired on September 29, 2027. After that date, existing v1 apps will stop running and will no longer handle requests or event-driven triggers.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for PowerShell 7.4 ends on November 10, 2026
item.description:
Support for PowerShell 7.4 ends on November 10, 2026. Azure Function apps using 7.4 will keep running, but security updates and customer support stop, so users should move to PowerShell 7.6.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for .NET 8 and .NET 9 ends on November 10, 2026—upgrade your apps to .NET 10
item.description:
Support for .NET 8 and .NET 9 in Azure Functions ends on November 10, 2026. Apps will keep running, but they will no longer receive security updates or support for those runtimes, so migrate to .NET 10 before the deadline.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for Node.js 22 ends on April 30, 2027
item.description:
Support for Node.js 22 in Azure Functions ends on April 30, 2027. Apps will keep running, but security patches, updates, and support for Node.js 22 will stop; move to Node.js 24 by then.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Functions support for PowerShell 7.6
item.description:
Azure Functions now generally supports PowerShell 7.6. Apps can be developed locally with PowerShell 7.6 and deployed to Azure Functions plans.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: TLS/SSL certificate and end-to-end TLS encryption support for Azure Functions Flex Consumption
item.description:
Azure Functions Flex Consumption now generally supports TLS/SSL certificates using a new site-scoped certificate model. It also adds end-to-end TLS encryption support for function apps in this plan.

  • Source: Azure Updates
